description: `hexa init --scaffold` and `hexa scaffold` emit a runnable, A+-graded Python counter skeleton, as they do for Rust, Go and TypeScript.

specs.description: --lang python writes the whole Python counter layout, with the package named after the project
specs.given: an empty directory and the project name `my-app`
specs.then: it writes exactly these files: `pyproject.toml`; the package `my_app/`, holding `__init__.py`, `domain/count.py`, `ports/store.py`, `usecases/increment.py`, `adapters/secondary/memory.py` and `composition_root.py`; `tests/__init__.py`; and `tests/test_increment.py`

specs.description: pyproject.toml declares the project, a version and the minimum Python
specs.given: the project name `my-app`, scaffolded with --lang python
specs.then: it has a `[project]` table with `name` set to the project's name, a non-empty `version`, and `requires-python = ">=3.10"`

specs.description: The port re-exports the domain's Count, and the test exercises the composition root
specs.given: a Python scaffold of `my-app`
specs.then: `ports/store.py` makes `Count` from the domain importable from the port, and `test_increment.py` is a unittest test case that obtains its use case through `my_app.composition_root`

specs.description: The in-memory adapter does not import the domain or the use cases
specs.given: a Python scaffold of `my-app`
specs.then: its only project-internal import is from `my_app.ports`; it imports nothing from `my_app.domain` or `my_app.usecases`

specs.description: No placeholder or template suffix survives in the Python output
specs.given: a Python scaffold of `my-app`
specs.when: every written path and file content is inspected
specs.then: no path or content contains `{{name}}` or `{{name_snake}}`, and no written file name ends in `.tmpl`

specs.description: The Python gate is unittest discovery and passes on a fresh scaffold
specs.given: a fresh Python scaffold of `my-app` and a `python3` of version 3.10 or later
specs.when: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` runs in the project root
specs.then: it exits 0, and its output reports `Ran 1 test` followed by `OK`

specs.description: SCAFFOLD_LANGS names python with its gate command
specs.given: the scaffold language table
specs.when: the entry for `python` is looked up
specs.then: its gate command is `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`

specs.description: The Python gate needs no install step and no network
specs.given: a fresh Python scaffold, with network access disabled and no third-party packages installed
specs.then: it passes; the gate command contains no `pip`, `install`, `venv` or `&&` step

specs.description: A failing unittest run does not count as a passing gate
specs.given: a Python scaffold whose test has been edited to fail
specs.when: the gate runs and the evidence reader reads its output
specs.then: the output reports `FAILED`, not `OK`, the gate exits non-zero, and the evidence reader does not record a pass

specs.description: Placeholders in an asset's path are rendered
specs.given: an asset at `scaffold/python/{{name_snake}}/domain/count.py.tmpl` and the project name `my-app`
specs.then: the file is written at `my_app/domain/count.py`

specs.description: {{name}} in a path is rendered to the name as given
specs.given: a test asset at `scaffold/<lang>/{{name}}.txt` and the project name `my-app`
specs.then: the file is written at `my-app.txt`

specs.description: No existing Rust, Go or TypeScript asset path holds a placeholder
specs.given: every embedded asset under `scaffold/rust/`, `scaffold/go/` and `scaffold/ts/`
specs.then: none contains `{{name}}` or `{{name_snake}}`

specs.description: Path rendering does not overwrite an existing file
specs.given: a directory that already holds `my_app/domain/count.py` with custom content
specs.then: `my_app/domain/count.py` keeps its custom content

specs.description: An asset's path is rendered by the same substitution as its contents
specs.given: any embedded asset under `scaffold/<lang>/` and any valid project name
specs.when: the scaffold computes the asset's output path
specs.then: the output path equals the asset's path with `{{name}}` and `{{name_snake}}` replaced exactly as they are replaced in its contents, and then its `.tmpl` suffix, if any, removed

specs.description: Python's ignore lines include __pycache__/ and .venv/
specs.given: the language `python`
specs.then: it contains `__pycache__/` and `.venv/`, together with `.hexa/loop.json`, `.hexa/loop.lock`, `.env*` and `!.env.example`

specs.description: Python's ignore lines are Python's only
specs.given: the languages `python`, `rust`, `ts` and `go`
specs.then: `python`'s lines contain no `target/`, `node_modules/` or `dist/`; and none of the `rust`, `ts` or `go` lines contain `__pycache__/` or `.venv/`

specs.description: A merged Python .gitignore always holds each Python line exactly once
specs.given: any existing `.gitignore` text, or none
specs.when: `merged_gitignore(existing, "python")` runs and its result (or the existing text, if the result is `None`) is read
specs.then: `__pycache__/` and `.venv/` each appear exactly once as a trimmed line, and every line of the existing text is kept in order

specs.description: hexa analyze grades the fresh Python scaffold A+ with full coverage
specs.given: a fresh Python scaffold of `my-app`
specs.then: the grade is A+; coverage has `classified == total` and an empty `unclassified` list; `violations`, `circular_deps` and `config_errors` are empty; and `composition_root.py` is classified as `HexLayer::CompositionRoot`

specs.description: The Python scaffold satisfies the domain policy it ships
specs.given: a fresh Python scaffold, with the domain policy it ships
specs.then: it reports no error-severity finding

specs.description: No Python scaffold file is left unclassified or in the wrong layer
specs.given: a fresh Python scaffold of `my-app`
specs.when: each file's layer is read from the analysis
specs.then: no file is `HexLayer::Unknown`; `domain/count.py` is Domain, `ports/store.py` is Ports, `usecases/increment.py` is Usecases, and `adapters/secondary/memory.py` is AdaptersSecondary

specs.description: A fresh Python scaffold needs no edit before its gate passes
specs.given: the scaffold output, exactly as written
specs.when: the Python gate runs without any file being modified
specs.then: it exits 0

specs.description: The Python scaffold is deterministic
specs.given: any valid project name and two empty directories
specs.when: the Python scaffold runs once in each directory with that name
specs.then: both runs write the same set of relative paths, with byte-identical contents

specs.description: --lang still defaults to rust
specs.given: an empty directory
specs.then: it writes the Rust scaffold and no Python file

specs.description: An unknown --lang is refused and names python among the known ones
specs.given: an empty directory
specs.then: it fails with a non-zero exit, writes no file, and its message names `python` alongside `rust`, `go` and `ts`

specs.description: The Rust, Go and TypeScript scaffolds are byte-for-byte unchanged
specs.given: any valid project name and each of the languages `rust`, `go` and `ts`
specs.when: the scaffold runs for that language
specs.then: the written paths and bytes equal what the scaffold wrote for that name and language before this ADR

specs.description: A module of the scaffolded package importing another is an internal import
specs.given: A fresh Python scaffold, with a new module in its domain that imports the domain's Count
specs.then: The import is read as one of the project's own (no import-policy finding for it), and the grade stays A+

amendments.reason: Fixture defects only, no assertion changed: S18 and S20 looked for each file's layer in hexa analyze --json, which names a file's layer only on a violation edge, so a clean scaffold showed none; they now ask the grade's own classifier (LayerMap::classify). S23 and S24 ran hexa scaffold without the description and --target it requires: S23 uses hexa init --scaffold (offline, the same --lang default), and S24 gives hexa scaffold its arguments, which refuses an unknown language before writing anything or calling a model. 23 fail without the fix, 24 pass with it
